arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case's counsel stated the facts were undisputed. He argued the officer did not violate the Fourth Amendment. He emphasized the nine-mile pursuit at high speeds.
the opposing side's counsel responded to questions about the proposed rule. He focused on the balance of risks. He argued the officer must consider harm to others and the suspect.
Justices probed the relevance of speed to potential death. They examined the scope of the case. They questioned the proposed balancing test for police force.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the limits of police force during a chase. It asks if an officer can end a dangerous pursuit by shooting the driver.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants a finding that the officer acted lawfully. He seeks dismissal of the liability claim.
the opposing side wants a finding that the officer violated the Fourth Amendment. He seeks personal liability for the officer.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the officer did not violate the Constitution. He claims the high-speed chase created a danger that justified the force.
the opposing side argues the officer used excessive force. He claims the officer failed to balance risks to the public and the suspect.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked if the fleeing driver caused the danger.

Justice Breyer questioned why the side that brought the case conceded certain points about the case scope. He noted the case involved many factors. He asked why the shopping center distraction mattered less than the speed. He asked if speed determined the likelihood of death. He asked if the rule requires balancing harm to others versus the fleeing person.

paragraphs: This case defines when police may use deadly force to end a chase. It sets the standard for officer liability in high-speed pursuits. It balances public safety against individual rights during emergencies.
